extracted.intended_audience: researchers and peer reviewers (especially early-career researchers) who want recognition and record-keeping for their peer review activity
extracted.subtask_description: Advice about using the Web of Science Reviewer Recognition Service (Publons) to get credit for peer review, indicate availability to review, track reviewed manuscripts, perform post-publication review, and export review records to ORCID. Geared toward reviewers seeking recognition and better workflow around peer-review contributions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Automatic recording of Royal Society reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Every review performed for a Royal Society journal can be automatically added to the reviewer’s Web of Science Reviewer Recognition Service profile, which they can use to showcase their contributions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This partnership (since 2017) means Royal Society reviewers' work is automatically recognised on the service; example statistic given: over 9,600 reviewers recognised for over 22k reviews. Use this auto-recording to build a verifiable public record of reviewing activity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indicate your interest to review for a journal
rubrics_metrics.description: You can indicate your interest to review for any partner journal in one click so editors can discover you for review invitations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designed to help early-career researchers who otherwise must wait to be invited after publishing. If your skills meet editors' needs, review requests could follow; the page links to a 'how it works' resource. Recommended as an active way to 'break into' peer review rather than passively waiting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Get recognition for helping your supervisor
rubrics_metrics.description: After adding a review to your profile you can invite collaborators using a privileged link; when a collaborator follows this link, they will have a copy of the review added to their profile so all contributors can be recognised.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addresses the common (but sometimes unrecognised) practice of senior researchers soliciting help from graduate students/post-docs when writing commissioned reviews. Use the collaborator-invite flow to ensure junior contributors receive formal recognition; feature supports fair attribution of hidden or delegated reviewing work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keep track of the manuscripts you reviewed post-publication
rubrics_metrics.description: The service sends you an email alert after the manuscript you reviewed (and received recognition for) has been published, telling you where it was published and including a link to the paper and its Altmetric score.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful to avoid the frustration of not knowing if a reviewed manuscript was published or how it was received. Use the alerts to follow up on outcomes and community attention; this is a tracking/monitoring feature rather than an evaluation rubric per se.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improve research with post-publication reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Web of Science Transparent Peer Review Service provides a platform for experts to critique, add to, or ask questions about research post-publication to help correct fraudulent or careless research that slipped through peer review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourages engagement in open post-publication critique as a means to improve research integrity and accelerate correction of the literature. The page frames this as a remedy for cases where traditional peer review failed and points readers to further information ('read more' link).

rubrics_metrics.name: Export your peer review records to ORCID
rubrics_metrics.description: Every verified review added to your Web of Science Reviewer Recognition Service record is automatically exported to your ORCID profile once you link both accounts; on ORCID each review is associated with a unique resolvable identifier linking back to the service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Promotes portability and verifiable attribution of reviewing work: ORCID integration (used by millions of researchers) lets the community confirm a review was verified and—if open—read it. The page notes you must link accounts (stepwise instructions referenced) to enable automatic export.
